articles.summary: Cornell’s president vowed to take a “serious look” at the role fraternities and sororities play in campus life as the “Cornell 7” case sparks a national reckoning over sex and drugs on American college campuses. For the first time since the investigation was reopened, University President Michael I. Kotlikoff directly addressed the scandal involving the Chi Phi fraternity house and a female student identified as “Jane Doe.” “What happened to Jane Doe in 2024 is deeply disturbing and will weigh heavily on our community for years to come,” Kotlikoff said in an eight-minute video statement. “My heart aches when I think of what she experienced.” “This has been one of the most difficult weeks in our history, and I know many of you are angry, saddened, and struggling, and that those bonds are under extraordinary stress,” he added. Kotlikoff said the unraveling scandal “raises heartbreaking and troubling issues” about the role party culture, alcohol, and drug use play in shaping the college experience. “At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship, and a powerful sense of community. articles.author: William Vaillancourt
articles.summary: Fox News Interior Secretary Doug Burgum made a gaffe on Monday during a Fox News interview, mistakenly saying he was in Venezuela instead of Louisiana. Burgum appeared on America Reports to discuss how Venezuela is shipping 15,000 tons of aluminum to the U.S. in a deal with Heeney Capital, a U.S. private investment firm, and Mercuria, a Swiss-founded energy trading company. The first shipment arrived Monday at the Port of Avondale in New Orleans. Burgum and two Louisiana members of Congress, Steve Scalise and Julia Letlow, were there to meet it. On Fox, Burgum, 70, spent about two minutes touting the benefits of the influx of aluminum from Venezuela before he misspoke. Read more at The Daily Beast.
